diffReview.scope: git diff bdb95d1..HEAD: under src only src/render/LookDev.js and one comment in src/app/NabdRuntime.js; no change in src/simulation, src/interaction, the event list or any pose, limit or privacy code, so the grab invariants (no penetration, 1.2 m/s and 280 deg/s caps, joint limits, privacy area, trunk bones) are untouched.
diffReview.threeR180Checked: Bundle read: onContextRestore (_e) sets C=false, saves at.autoReset and the Se shadow settings, calls N() (initGLContext), which assigns v.shadowMap=Se and v.info=at to new objects; render() returns at once while C is true; three's canvas listeners are added in the constructor, before createLookDev adds its own. The fix's assumptions match.
findings: No correctness bug found in installRenderCounters/createGpuTimer: info is read at every use; the shadow map is re-wrapped on the restore event and before every render; the dead map gets its own render back; frames issued while lost go to lostFrames and leave frames/shadowUpdates/last-frame alone; the GPU timer neither creates nor polls queries while lost, drops old-context queries on reset() without passing them to the new context, and ignores non-finite results.
Hot path cost per render: two identity compares and two gl.isContextLost() calls, only under ?qa; nothing runs without ?qa.

No leftover debug code; LF everywhere (the 4 hits of a CR byte are JPEGs); git diff --check clean; no Co-Authored-By or other trailer; no junk files; Q1 evidence 1,219,479 bytes and 6 JPEGs before this round, about 1.45 MB and still 6 JPEGs after it.
Cosmetic: the cd7a47a body ends with 'no picture change (pixel diff below)' but no pixel diff follows in that body (it is listed under Checks).

webkitSecondLossAttribution.question: Is 'WebKit loses the restored context again by itself' caused by Q1 code?
webkitSecondLossAttribution.method: scripts/restore-hang-rate.mjs: base 0a87bd7 (no LookDev at all), old bdb95d1 and HEAD served side by side, rotated per trial, 8 trials each, one forced loseContext/restoreContext per fresh page.
webkitSecondLossAttribution.conclusion: The tree without any Q1 code shows the same second loss, so it is WebKit-on-Windows behaviour, not Q1's. HEAD is not worse than base. The WebKit 'drawBuffers: more than max draw buffers' error appeared in 4 of 5 old and 1 of 2 HEAD second-loss sessions and in 0 of 2 base ones; LookDev issues no drawBuffers call (its only GL calls are timer queries, unused in WebKit where the extension is absent), so it comes from three's own state path during the loss; the base sample is small.

nonBlocking: WebKit Q1-c can fail its first attempt when WebKit loses the restored context a second time (1 of 7 first attempts in this round, 2 of 2 in the implementer's runs; restore-hang-rate: 2 of 7 HEAD pages). The retry covers it, but both attempts can fail (about 2-11 % of WebKit runs for a per-attempt rate of 14-33 %, the range of these samples) and Q2+ will inherit that. Consider having Q1-c skip with an annotation when 'WebGL: context lost.' follows three's 'Context Restored' in WebKit, instead of failing.

App behaviour outside Q1 (pre-existing, same code in base): after a context loss the page keeps its 'reload' notice and #model-status 'error'; in Chrome, clicking #forearm-practice after a forced restore did not start the drill within 25 s. Needs a product decision (the implementer raised it too).
WebKit boot hangs (U21) remain and are not Q1's: smoke 2 flaky (S8, V2), pixel-diff retries base 3 / work 3, restore-hang-rate not ready base 2/8, old 0/8, HEAD 1/8.

Programs count after a restore is lower than before (V2 20 -> 18, V4 22 -> 20): three recompiles lazily on the new context and the readout reports the live count. Expected, but a later cluster comparing render.programs must not compare across a restore.
